/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 28 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3268 (-158)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5351 (-433)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2402 (-5)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1790 (4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1012 (1)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize sector gave back more than the gains achieved last week, beginning the week on a weaker footing. The BCI 182 5TC fell by $3,930 to $48,527, with both basins losing ground particularly on the transpacific round voyage. While little fresh activity from Brazil had emerged by the time of publication, offers were said to be lower than last week against a backdrop of limited bidding interest. The C3 index declined by $1.741 to $40.659, with the index window now fully rolling into the second half of October. Activity in the Pacific appeared busier at the start of the week ahead of China's Golden Week holiday. However, it failed to translate into a higher fixing level with the C5 index retreating from $15.625 to $14.335. Market rumours suggested that Rio Tinto fixed 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao for 14/16 October at $14.40, while BHP was also rumoured to have fixed 160,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao over the same loading window at $14.35. Last week, Vale took a TBN for 170,000/10 TRMT to Son Duong 5/7 October at a rate in the low/mid $9s.
PANAMAX
Brokers expressed mixed views on the trans-Atlantic market today, although the P1A posted a modest gain. Trading activity was described as relatively subdued, with Charterers reportedly pausing to reassess market fundamentals. As a result, the bid-offer spread remains wide, supported by continued Owner optimism on rates. Market participants also noted improving demand from the US Gulf, which is helping to underpin fronthaul levels. In the Pacific, sentiment remains cautious as market participants prepare for the upcoming Golden Week holidays in China. Indonesian demand is reported to be relatively quiet, with some suggesting that Owners are holding back offers while seeking greater clarity on market direction. The scrubber-fitted Star Virginia (81,061 2015) open Singapore 30 September/1 October was fixed for a trip via Indonesia to India, although further details were not reported. The Shandong Xin De (82,152 2024) open Hong Kong 2/3 October fixed a voyage stem from Australia to China. Elsewhere, Cobelfret was said to have covered its alumina backhaul stem from Bunbury to Iceland for 15/21 October loading dates, while Mirabulk covered an iron ore cargo from Geraldton to Qingdao for loading on 19/22 October. Overall, reported fixture activity was fairly limited today as the P5TC slipped by $42 to $21,620.
SUPRAMAX
An especially slow start to the new week, after disruption from holidays in the East and ABSA in Miami last week, the 11TC average started the week up $41 to settle $22,620. The Sunisa Naree (63,345 2016) Phuket 27 September was reported fixed for 11 to 13 months index linked 103% of the BSI to PACC Line and the Jewel of Shinas (55,877 2011) CJK 4-7 October was said to be on subjects for 5 to 7 months at $18,000, but no Charterer was mentioned. The Truong Minh Success (61,346 2014) Campha 30 September-1 October fixed a trip Bangladesh intention clinker at a strong $33,000 and the Astrid Schulte (61,255 2017) Richards Bay 5 October was reported fixed basis delivery Port Elizabeth for a trip East coast India at $27,000 plus $270,000 ballast bonus, although an informed source said the details were incorrect, the Van Infinity (56,593 2011) prompt in Sohar fixed to West coast India at $20,000 and the Jin Xing (55,496 2007) Djibouti 22-23 September did a trip via Aqaba to East coast India at around $18-19,000 with Jaldhi, however another source suggested the rate was $21,000.
HANDYSIZE
The week opened on a relatively quiet and mixed note, with sentiment remaining largely positional. The BHSI closed at 1,012, while the 7TC average edged up by $18 to finish at $18,208. The Continent and Mediterranean remained supported by fresh demand, resulting in a modest increase in rates. Across the South Atlantic and US Gulf, changes were limited and the market appeared broadly balanced, with rates edging slightly above last-done levels as underlying fundamentals remained largely unchanged. In contrast, the Pacific market started the week on a slightly softer note, with little change in market conditions and no clear direction emerging.

Market Fundamentals
JFE Steel Production

Japan’s second-largest steel producer, JFE Steel, expects to lose ~0.6 Mt of steel output at its Chiba plant following heavy rainfall in August, with further flooding from Typhoon Dujuan in September affecting other facilities, the company announced on Friday. The company anticipates operations in Chiba to normalise by mid-October at the earliest, McCloskey reports. In its latest quarterly report, JFE estimated consolidated 2q26 crude steel production at 5.9 Mt, up 0.1 Mt from the same period in the year prior.

China Revises US Farm Trade Tariffs

China's commerce ministry and the White House jointly issued a tariff-reduction list on Monday covering US corn, wheat, sorghum, soyoil, soymeal, meat and dairy, following last week's Xi-Trump summit in Washington, Reuters reports. Soybeans, China's largest US farm import, still face an additional 10% tariff, a cost traders say private crushers are unable to absorb. State buyers Sinograin and COFCO have taken over 12 Mt of US soybeans, nearly half of the 25 Mt annual commitment cited by the White House, though this remains unconfirmed by China. In the year to 17 September, soybean exports to China stood 5.9 Mt higher on the year at 12.4 Mt, USDA data show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw another volatile session, with a sharp early fall followed by a partial afternoon recovery. October opened around 45,500 before dropping quickly through 44,000 and eventually reaching 42,250. It recovered later, with good volume around 42,700–43,000 into the close. November fell from 42,750 to around 41,400 before recovering toward 41,900–42,100. December moved from 41,250–41,350 down to 40,250 before recovering to 41,000. Q4 26 fell from 42,650 to 41,250–41,500 before recovering to 42,100 late. Q1 27 traded from 30,100 down to 29,500, recovering to 30,000. On the back end cal 27 traded 32,450 early doors to 32,650 later on, while cal 28 printed at a low of 27,400 up to 27,550. Overall, the morning weakness gave way to a meaningful late recovery, although the front end remained below opening levels.
